name: Create a QDoc
description:
# Context

This design covers UC-1, Create a QDoc, in a green field: a quality manager starts a quality document, the QDoc System numbers it, creates version 1 with an empty content file and tells the other quality managers (UC-1). The drivers:

- **The subsystem structure** of the QDoc System: value-stream subsystems such as Preparation, platform subsystems such as Notifications and Identity that hold no process of their own (QDoc System structure).
- **Who may create, and what a new QDoc must hold:** only quality managers (SR-PRE-001); a title, a type from the list and at least one author (FR-PRE-001, FR-PRE-002); an active QDoc with a number and version 1 in the status new with one empty content file (FR-PRE-003 to FR-PRE-005, FR-PRE-009); never a QDoc without a version (FR-PRE-010).
- **Every quality manager learns of each new QDoc** (FR-NOT-001), within a delay still open (TBD-01).

# Decisions

## D1. One bounded context per subsystem, only the two UC-1 needs

The new root [qdocmanagement](noesis:module|qdocmanagement) holds one module per subsystem, each its own bounded context. UC-1 needs [preparation](noesis:module|qdocmanagement.preparation) and [notifications](noesis:module|qdocmanagement.notifications); the others arrive with the use cases that need them.

- **Why:** the structure document already splits the system and gives each subsystem its area code; following it keeps requirement ids and modules aligned.
- **Trade-off:** Identity is reached through a port of the context that needs it rather than a shared module (D3).

## D2. QDoc is the aggregate, and owns its versions

[QDoc](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.QDoc) is the aggregate root; [Version](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.Version) and [ContentFile](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.ContentFile) are entities inside it. [QDoc.create](noesis:behavior|qdocmanagement.preparation.QDoc.create) makes an active QDoc together with its first version, from [Version.createFirst](noesis:behavior|qdocmanagement.preparation.Version.createFirst).

- **Why:** creating a QDoc is creating its version 1 (FR-PRE-004), and "at least one version" (FR-PRE-010) is an invariant only the QDoc can keep. A QDoc's own status is active or archived; workflow statuses belong to versions.
- **Trade-off:** the whole QDoc is loaded and saved together ([QDocRepository](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.QDocRepository)). Here a content file only exists: its editing, history and comments belong to Content management (UC-4).

## D3. An application service runs the use case and announces it atomically

[QDocCreationService.createQDoc](noesis:behavior|qdocmanagement.preparation.QDocCreationService.createQDoc) takes a [CreateQDoc](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.CreateQDoc) command, checks the requester's role through the [IdentityProvider](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.IdentityProvider) port, takes a number from [DocumentNumberGenerator](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.DocumentNumberGenerator), creates the QDoc, saves it and publishes [QDocCreated](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.QDocCreated) through [PreparationEventPublisher](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.PreparationEventPublisher) in one unit of work.

- **Why:** the role check is a security rule at the boundary (SR-PRE-001) and needs the Identity subsystem; the number is required from the start (FR-PRE-009) but its format is UC-2's, so it sits behind a domain service of its own.
- **Saved and announced together:** either both happen or neither, so no quality manager hears of a QDoc that does not exist.

## D4. Notifications is a generic service; Preparation decides who is told

The [notifications](noesis:module|qdocmanagement.notifications) context knows nothing of QDocs. [NotificationService.notifyUsers](noesis:behavior|qdocmanagement.notifications.NotificationService.notifyUsers) takes a [NotifyUsers](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.notifications.NotifyUsers) request naming the recipients, a subject and a body, and sends each recipient a [Notification](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.notifications.Notification) through [NotificationSender](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.notifications.NotificationSender); a failed delivery to one stops no other. `createQDoc` finds the quality managers through [IdentityProvider.findQualityManagers](noesis:behavior|qdocmanagement.preparation.IdentityProvider.findQualityManagers), builds the [NewQDocNotification](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.NewQDocNotification) and asks Notifications to deliver it (FR-NOT-001).

- **Why:** Notifications is a platform subsystem with no process of its own (structure); as an open host it serves new versions and assignments the same way, without learning each caller's language.
- **Trade-off:** every subsystem that wants someone told composes the message and picks the recipients itself. `QDocCreated` is still published for whoever follows new QDocs. The channel and the maximum delay are TBD-01.

## D5. People are assigned as given, until UC-3

Version 1 holds an [Assignment](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.Assignment) for each author named in the request, and for each reviewer and approver if any are named (FR-PRE-006 to FR-PRE-008).

- **Why:** the checks on assignees (role held, active account) are UC-3's; reviewers and approvers are optional because they can be added later, and an approver is needed only when a version is shared (UC-6).
- **Trade-off:** until UC-3, a request can assign someone who would fail those checks.

## D6. Closed vocabularies are value objects

[QDocTitle](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.QDocTitle) is never blank; [DocumentType](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.DocumentType), [QDocStatus](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.QDocStatus), [VersionStatus](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.VersionStatus) and [AssignmentRole](noesis:building_block|qdocmanagement.preparation.AssignmentRole) each take one value from their list.

- **Why:** FR-PRE-001 and FR-PRE-002; the glossary fixes each list. The document types may grow, which is a change to that list, not to any QDoc.

# How they connect

D1 decides where each piece lives; D2 decides what one transaction holds; D3 orchestrates within Preparation and, through D4, has the quality managers told. D5 and D6 are what D2 and D3 check today, leaving the rest to UC-2 and UC-3.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  accTitle: Creating a QDoc and telling the quality managers
  actor QM as Quality manager
  participant S as QDocCreationService
  participant I as IdentityProvider
  participant N as DocumentNumberGenerator
  participant Q as QDoc
  participant R as QDocRepository + PreparationEventPublisher
  participant NS as NotificationService
  QM->>S: createQDoc(CreateQDoc)
  S->>I: isQualityManager(requester)
  S->>N: next(documentType)
  S->>Q: create(command, number)
  Q-->>S: QDocCreated (version 1 inside)
  S->>R: save + publish, one unit of work
  S->>I: findQualityManagers()
  S->>NS: notifyUsers(NewQDocNotification)
  NS->>NS: send to each recipient, failures isolated
```

# Left out and open

- The document number's format, sequence and uniqueness: UC-2.
- Role and active-account checks on assignees: UC-3.
- Editing, history and comments of content files: UC-4, in Content management.
- The notification channel and its maximum delay: TBD-01.

diagram.value:
sequenceDiagram
  accTitle: Notifying users on another subsystem's request
  participant Caller as Calling subsystem
  Caller->>NotificationService: notifyUsers(command)
  loop each recipient
    NotificationService->>NotificationSender: send(Notification)
  end
